_doc: The 1904 district's front yards (T-3203): foundation shrubs along each house lot's front and the first metres of its sides, low beds in the lawn before the house, and creeper where a picture shows it. GENERATED by tools/plant_prairie_1904_front_yards.py from data/street_grid/1904.json, the 1904 sidecars' baked models and the traced Sanborn footprints -- do not hand-edit; re-run the tool. Local ENU metres of data/datum.json. shrubs: [e, n, radius_m, height_m, form, tone, (grade if not the lot's)]; beds: [e, n, half_length_m, half_width_m, heading_deg, kind, palette]; creeper: [e, n, facing_deg, width_m, height_m]. The lawn is the ground's own sward.

clipped.name: clipped evergreen
clipped.note: a sheared, rounded foundation shrub (box, yew or arborvitae kept low)

mound.name: flowering shrub
mound.note: a loose deciduous mound (spiraea, hydrangea, snowball, barberry)

tall.name: tall shrub
tall.note: a lilac or syringa grown up at a corner of the house

beds.round: a round bed cut in the lawn

placement.note: Shrubs stand 0.45-0.95 m off the house's walls, clear of the lot line, its boundary, every stoop, pier and paved walk, and of a 2.7 m way from each front door straight to the lot line; beds stand in the open lawn before the house. Seeded by the parcel's id.

creeper.note: Ivy over the west front and the porch, to about the second storey's sills and past them on the porch's piers (both Detroit Publishing views).

border.note: A dense border of shrubs inside the coping along 18th Street, east of the house (LC-D4-4a08066, right of the house).

creeper.note: Ivy over the north part of the front and the round bay to the third storey in the photograph; the print shows an electric lamp, so it is after 1904, and ivy of that reach was growing years before it.
